facts.text: I've been feeling sick to my stomach.
It's been going on for about a month.

facts.item: how long the nausea and vomiting have been going on
aliases: how long the symptoms have been going on
facts.text: The nausea and vomiting started 5 days ago.
For about a month I haven't had much appetite.
I've lost 6 kg over the past month without trying.
Over the past month I've had occasional vague belly pain.
My skin has recently become more tanned.
I've had an underactive thyroid for 17 years.
For years I took levothyroxine, and my thyroid was well controlled on it.
Several months ago I switched from levothyroxine to animal thyroid extract.
A week ago I started trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, 160 mg twice a day.
I have a sinus infection; that is what I started the antibiotic for a week ago.

findings.name: metabolic panel
findings.result: Sodium 101 mmol/L; chloride 73 mmol/L; potassium 5.2 mmol/L; CO2 16 mmol/L; BUN 20 mg/dL; creatinine 0.8 mg/dL; calcium normal; phosphorus normal; glucose normal; albumin normal.

gold.reasoning: 1. Consideration of nonhypotonic hyponatremia was excluded — “Since hyperglycemia and other causes of nonhypotonic hyponatremia were excluded, our patient had hypotonic hypovolemic hyponatremia.” 2. Diuretic-induced hyponatremia was ruled out — “…no history of diuretic use…” 3. Hypothyroidism was considered a minor contributor — “we also believe that inadequately controlled hypothyroidism due to self‐switching from levothyroxine to animal thyroid extract … may have played a minor role in the development of the hyponatremia.” 4. TMP-SMX was identified as an acute exacerbating factor — “this situation was acutely exacerbated by TMP‐SMX use several days prior.”

f003: Fatigue appears both in the 5-day presentation (s001) and the 1-month history (s002); one fact with the longer duration.
f012: The reasoning calls this a self-switch; the prompt says only 'she switched', so the text does not say who decided.

source_issues: Urine sodium (128 mmol/L) and urine osmolality (128 mOsm/kg) have the same number, which may be a copying error.
Cortisol and ACTH results are not given; s012 only says adrenal function tests were ordered.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with 5 days of nausea, vomiting and fatigue on a background of a month of poor appetite, weight loss, vague abdominal pain and skin tanning (s001-s009).
s011 is cited only for 'no history of diuretic use' (f015); its diagnostic label (hypotonic hypovolemic hyponatremia) is the clinician's interpretation and is not a finding.
Calcium, phosphorus, glucose and albumin are grouped with the metabolic panel; liver function tests and the lipid panel are separate records.
The sinus infection (f014) is recent history before the index visit; the TMP-SMX started for it is a medication fact.

excluded_sentences.reason: Clinician's reasoning (hyperglycemia and nonhypotonic hyponatremia excluded); no result is given beyond the normal glucose already in x008.
Clinician's reasoning naming adrenal insufficiency (narrative_conclusion); adrenal function tests were ordered but no results are given.
